# Disjoint arc bumps give one positive-semidefinite stress for any finite number of groups

This is a conditional local theorem. It assumes a stable planar support arc
with strictly positive curvature and C2 selected cap quantiles. It makes no
global smoothness, finite-contact-arc, or polytopal-attainment claim.

## 1. Exact hypotheses and notation

Let a positive finite compatible planar fiber family have total mixed area M
and locally minimal maximum depth beta>0. Let I be an open interval of
continuous normal angles. Every support function h_z is C2 on I and its
curvature radius r_z=h_z+h_z'' is strictly positive there.

On I assume a fixed finite list of active support compatibility equalities

    sum_z a_lz h_z(theta)=0

holds identically; all other compatibility inequalities have a strict gap
on each compact subinterval used below. Put

    L={v:sum_z a_lz v_z=0 for every active l}.

The usual finite-base Jensen support constraints have precisely this linear
form with coefficients independent of theta. Consequently r(theta) belongs
to L. Signed compactly supported perturbations

    delta h_z(theta)=v_z phi(theta),   v in L, phi in C_c^infinity(I),

preserve the active equalities exactly. Finite sums remain convex and
compatible for small |t|: their second derivatives are bounded on compact
supports where every r_z has a positive lower bound, and the inactive gaps
are uniform there. No signed perturbation on a zero-curvature arc is claimed.

Choose ANY one critical cap circuit at EVERY globally deepest integer index,
and a slack circuit at every other index. There are finitely many selected
caps. Assume that on each z-fiber boundary arc with normal in I each selected
cap has a constant strict membership indicator I_ijz in {0,1}. All perturbed
regions then remain wholly inside or wholly outside that cap. Finally assume
the selected cap masses are C2 in the body parameters and thresholds near
the chosen configuration, with positive section masses S_ij. Absence of
cap crossings merely on I does NOT by itself imply this last hypothesis;
coincidences elsewhere must be excluded or separately treated.

Write rho_ij for each positive circuit and put

    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_k rho_ik/S_ik),
    c_iz=sum_j theta_ij I_ijz.

Let f_i=tau_i/M be the exact normalized quantile-cover comparison from
candidate a0fdd477aa859374, and g_i=df_i. These selected f_i cover
all deepest sites, not only a smaller first-order essential block.

## 2. Area and cap Hessians on a stable arc

The planar support area formula gives, for one perturbation v phi,

    M'=sum_z v_z integral r_z phi,
    M''=Q(phi) sum_z v_z^2,
    Q(phi)=integral_I(phi^2-phi'^2).

Because each cap indicator is constant on the changed region,

    F_ij'=sum_z I_ijz v_z integral r_z phi,
    F_ij''=Q(phi) sum_z I_ijz v_z^2.                         (1)

Choose phi orthogonal to EVERY r_z. Then all first masses vanish. Every
first quantile threshold derivative is therefore zero. Formula (1) of
candidate a0a4e151af2d0678 has no mixed-threshold or
threshold-square term, and gives

    f_i''=(-Q(phi)) q_i(v),
    q_i(v)=(1/M)sum_z (beta-c_iz)v_z^2.                     (2)

Thus the sign in the eventual area stress is fixed, not inferred by analogy
with a first-order argument.

There is always a nonzero such phi on any subinterval J compactly contained
in I. Take |P|+1 smooth bumps with pairwise disjoint supports in J and solve
the |P| homogeneous orthogonality equations. If J has length less than pi,
then Q(phi)<0. An elementary proof of the needed Poincare estimate uses
w(theta)=sin(pi(theta-a)/|J|): for a compactly supported phi,

    integral(phi'^2-(pi/|J|)^2 phi^2)
        =integral w^2[(phi/w)']^2 >=0.

Rescaling phi gives any prescribed negative value of Q.

## 3. Disjoint supports convexify the whole joint Hessian image

For any finite list v_1,...,v_N in L and weights t_a>=0, choose pairwise
disjoint compact subintervals J_a of I. On each choose phi_a orthogonal to
all r_z and normalized by Q(phi_a)=-t_a. Set

    delta h_z=sum_a (v_a)_z phi_a.

All first masses still vanish. Cross second variations vanish because the
supports of phi_a and all their derivatives are disjoint. Therefore the
joint Hessian vector of the selected normalized covers is EXACTLY

    sum_a t_a q(v_a),       q(v)=(q_i(v))_i.                 (3)

Each finite conic sum is realized by one admissible finite perturbation.
There is no need for a limiting infinite collection of bumps or a uniform
small-t bound over infinitely many choices.

Let U be the linear space of arc-supported compatible support variations
just described, and G(U)={(g_i(a))_i:a in U}. One may enlarge U by other
directions only when the combined paths
h+t delta h+(t^2/2)a are explicitly feasible in a C2 parameter chart.
Using U itself requires no such additional chart assumption.

If an element of

    cone{q(v):v in L}+G(U)                                  (4)

were strictly negative in every coordinate, realize its conic part by (3)
and use its U-component as an order-t^2 acceleration. Every selected deepest
quantile cover would have mass ratio strictly below beta for small nonzero
t, while the nondeep covers remain slack. This contradicts local minimality.

The convex cone (4) is therefore disjoint from the open negative orthant.
Separating it from that OPEN set gives a nonzero vector pi>=0 such that

    sum_i pi_i g_i=0 on U,
    sum_i pi_i q_i(v)>=0 for every v in L.                   (5)

Normalize sum pi_i=1. Closure of the cone is not required for separation
from an open convex set. Since the cone contains0, is closed under positive
scaling, and contains both signs of G(U), separation yields exactly the
homogeneous inequalities and annihilation in (5).

## 4. The fixed diagonal stress and curvature nullspace

Define one common collection of cap multipliers and arc weights by

    lambda_ij=pi_i theta_ij/beta,
    W_z=1-sum_ij lambda_ij I_ijz.

These satisfy sum lambda_ij=1/beta. Equations (2),(5) give

    sum_z W_z v_z^2 >=0             for every v in L.        (6)

The same pi annihilates ALL first variations in U. Thus, for every v in L
and every compact smooth test function phi,

    integral phi(theta) sum_z W_z r_z(theta)v_z dtheta=0.

The integrand is continuous, so

    sum_z W_z r_z(theta)v_z=0       for all v in L, theta in I. (7)

The curvature vector r(theta) already belongs to L. It therefore lies in
the fixed nullspace of the positive-semidefinite form (6) restricted to L.
Both the first-order annihilation and second-order semidefiniteness use the
SAME stress; no arbitrary pre-existing first-order multiplier was promoted
to a Hessian condition.

For example, if L={(a,b,(a+b)/2)} and W=(1,1,-2), the form is
(a-b)^2/2. Its nullspace is the line a=b, so all three curvature radii agree
on I. More generally a one-dimensional nullspace forces fixed positive
curvature ratios, hence locally translated homothetic support arcs.

This is an arbitrary-finite-group result; it needs neither a two-site
restriction nor Dines' theorem. It remains conditional on the explicit
stable-arc, positive-curvature, and C2-quantile hypotheses above. The
nonsmooth cap-quantile extension is not asserted here.
